covers: rmodels.c's LoadMaterialDefault (its maps' colors, values and textures, the diffuse map's raylib's default texture, its shader and params), IsMaterialValid on it and on materials without maps, a shader or both, UnloadMaterial on a material given a texture on two maps, the texture unloaded first: the default shader and texture kept, the texture freed; a model given a texture, the texture unloaded, then the model (UnloadTexture, UnloadModel): the texture freed; a texture two loads of a glTF file share, read from the second after UnloadMaterial frees the first's material (its base color and normal maps, which 5.5's LoadGLTF reads as 6.2's)
notes: Only what raylib and helix-raylib do alike is here (docs/DECISIONS.md 25): raylib frees a texture at UnloadTexture and UnloadModel frees none, where helix-raylib frees it when the last of its holders lets go, so a texture given to a material or model is freed after both on either side. raylib's C sees a texture freed by GL taking its name again for the next texture made; helix-raylib's harness by its pixels being gone. The model is materials_62's (its makematerials.py); only UnloadModel's and UnloadMaterial's effect on it is printed here, its materials' contents there. The default texture is read back after the unload on both sides.
